! ==========================================================================
! This file sets the different technical parameters intrinsic to the
! FKS program and which controls the behaviour of the code at run
! time.  The common user should not edit this file and only experts
! should venture editing these parameters.
! ==========================================================================
!
! ==========================================================================
! Parameters controlling the tests based on the IR poles comparison
! ==========================================================================
!
! This threshold sets the limiting value for the comparison of the
! relative difference of the IR pole from the OLP and the one computed
! internaly by MadFKS.  The value below is used for the first PS
! points to assess the sanity of the computation. A value ten times
! smaller will be used for the systematic check of IR poles at
! runtime.
! Notice that the systematic comparison of IR poles at run time is
! only performed when the Monte-Carlo over helicity configurations
! method is not used.  Set this value to '-1.0d0' if you want the
! check to always pass.
#IRPoleCheckThreshold
1.0d-5
! Default :: 1.0d-5
!
! ==========================================================================
! OLP (virtuals) behavior at run time
! ==========================================================================
!
!
! Set the precision required from the OLP code. The IR poles check
! will be performed at run time with a threshold ten times loser than
! the value below. When equal to '-1d0' the default value of the OLP
! is used, and the poles check is disabled at run time
!
#PrecisionVirtualAtRunTime
1.0d-3
! Default :: 1.0d-3
!
! ==========================================================================
! Parameters controlling what coupling orders must be factorized by the
! contributions included by MadFKS in the context of mixed-order expansions
! ==========================================================================
!
! Set the QCD and QED squared order that must be factorized by the  
! contribution selected. This follows the same convention as the syntax 
! QCD^2== and QED^2== used at generation time. The default value of -1 
! instructs MadFKS to include all those available.
!
#QCD^2==
-1
! Default :: -1
!
#QED^2==
-1
! Default :: -1
!
! Alternatively the user can defined a list of squared orders to select
! The first entry is the number of specifed squared orders, and the ordering
! is indicated in orders.inc with typically QCD first, followed by QED
! This is just the generalization of the short-hand above.
!
! Example:
!
! #SelectedCouplingOrders
! 2
! 4 0
! 2 2
!
! Selects all contribution factorizing \alpha_s^2 and \alpha_s * \alpha.
!
#SelectedCouplingOrders
0
-1 -1
! Default ::
! 0
! -1 -1
!
! ==========================================================================
! This parameter allows to veto of select specific type of contributions.
!     type=1 : real-emission
!     type=2 : Born
!     type=3 : integrated counter terms
!     type=4 : soft counter-term
!     type=5 : collinear counter-term
!     type=6 : soft-collinear counter-term
!     type=7 : O(alphaS) expansion of Sudakov factor for NNLL+NLO
!     type=8 : soft counter-term (with n+1-body kin.)
!     type=9 : collinear counter-term (with n+1-body kin.)
!     type=10: soft-collinear counter-term (with n+1-body kin.)
!     type=11: real-emission (with n-body kin.)
!     type=12: MC subtraction with n-body kin.
!     type=13: MC subtraction with n+1-body kin.
!     type=14: virtual corrections
!     type=15: virt-trick: average born contribution
! ==========================================================================
! 
! The first entry specifies the length  of the list of vetoed or allowed types
!
! Example:
! #SelectedContributionTypes
! 3
! 2 14 15
!
! Would select only the finite part of the virtual and the Born contribution, and
!
! #VetoedContributionTypes
! 1
! 2
!
! Would remove the Born contribution, effectively computing only the NLO contribs.
!
! The default values disable completely these filters.
!
#VetoedContributionTypes
0
-1
! Default ::
! 0
! -1
!
#SelectedContributionTypes
0
-1
! Default :: .true.
! 0
! -1
!
! ==========================================================================
! Parameters defining the techniques used for the MC integration
! ==========================================================================
!
! This integer sets what is the minimum number of contributing
! helicities (in a given subrpocess) which is necessary for MadFKS to
! switch to the Monte-Carlo over helicity configurations method. Set
! this to '-1' if you want to forbid the use of this method
! altogether.
#NHelForMCoverHels
4
! Default :: 4
!
! This parameter sets for which fraction of the events the virtual
! matrix elements should be included. When using MINT, during the
! grid-setup phase, this number will be updated automatically after
! each iteration depending on the relative MC uncertainties.
#VirtualFraction
1.0d0
! Default :: 1.0d0
!
! This parameter sets the minimal fraction of the events for which the
! virtual matrix elements should be included.
#MinVirtualFraction
0.005d0
! Default :: 0.005d0
!
! Use a polynomial fit for the virtual corrections. Gets a better accuracy,
! but uses more memmory and disk space.
#UsePolyVirtual
.False.
! Default :: .True.
!
! ==========================================================================
! Combination of matrix elements
! ==========================================================================
!
! For fixed order calculations only (ignored for (N)LO+PS runs): This
! parameter determines if parton flavour configurations with idential
! matrix elements should be separated at the level of the analysis or
! not (these contributions are typically added together in
! parton_lum_?.f files and only the PDG info of the first contribution
! is passed to the analysis). This can be useful to tag e.g. b-jets in
! the case of a 5FS calculation. [Warning: in this case jets that
! contain both a b quark and a bbar quark should not be considered
! b-jet]. Setting this to .true. makes the code slower, in particular
! for complicated analyses as well as when doing reweighting for many
! scales and PDFs sets, since they have to be done for each flavour
! configuration separately.
#SeparateFlavourConfigurations
.false.
! Default :: .false.
!
! ==========================================================================
! Mapping for initial-state FKS emitters
! ==========================================================================
!
! 0: automatic (currently the asymmetric mapping in all run modes).
! 1: the original symmetric mapping, available without shower matching.
! 2: the asymmetric, Pythia-like mapping (only the emitting Bjorken x changes).
! A forced symmetric mapping with shower matching is rejected. The same
! choice is used for the real point, its counterevents, inverse projection,
! and the lepton recoil chart without event projection.
#FKSISRMapping
0
! Default :: 0
!
! ==========================================================================
! Recoil choice for final-state FKS emitters
! ==========================================================================
!
! 0: use the resonance's final-state decay system when available, or
!    the complete final-state recoil system otherwise (default).
! 1: use incoming particle 1 as the local recoiler.
! 2: use incoming particle 2 as the local recoiler.
! Initial-state recoil requires two incoming particles and a massless
! selected parton from a hadron beam (abs(lpp)=1 or 2). Its Bjorken x
! increases during radiation; the other final-state spectators keep
! their momenta. This option is supported for fixed-order calculations.
! Initial-state emitters keep their ordinary FKS map.
#FKSFinalRecoil
0
! Default :: 0
!
! ==========================================================================
! MC@NLO construction
! ==========================================================================
!
! Upper photon-conversion mass in PYTHIA8 QED MC subtraction (GeV).
! The shower launch script uses the same value for TimeShower:mMaxGamma.
! Rerun integration/grid setup after changing this setting.
#Pythia8MMaxGamma
10d0
! Default :: 10d0
!
! Use the refactored MC@NLO construction.  In this mode the complete
! explicit sum over native (kl) histories is formed before multiplying
! H-event subtraction terms by the outer S_ij function.
! Set .false. to use the standard native-sector MC@NLO matching.
#MCExplicitKLSum
.true.
! Default :: .true.
!
! Choose how Born colour flows enter the MC@NLO subtraction in both
! H and S events. With .true., evaluate at a sampled Born flow and apply
! its sampling weight (the current prescription). With .false., explicitly
! sum the MC counterterms over Born flows before combining event weights.
! The flow sum uses this branch's matching kernels and phase-space maps;
! it does not restore all matching choices of the 3.x series.
! Event colours and shower scales use this branch's sampled Born owner;
! the sum includes each flow's soft replacement and MC@NLO-Delta factor.
! Summed mode costs one native evaluation per leading Born flow.
! Independent of MCExplicitKLSum and FKSExplicitSum. Ignored at fixed order.
! Rerun integration/grid setup after changing this setting.
#MCSubtractionAtFixedFlow
.true.
! Default :: .true.
!
! Explicitly sum the outer FKS configurations at each integration point
! in NLO+PS runs, instead of sampling a group of configurations. The Born
! contribution is included once; S-event terms are combined before taking
! absolute values for unweighting. This can reduce negative weights at the
! cost of more matrix-element evaluations per point. Uses a common Born
! sampling chart so that the S events have identical underlying momenta.
! Any separate initial/final-state integration channels remain separate.
! Independent of MCExplicitKLSum (the inner matching-history sum).
! Requires event projection. Ignored at fixed order; not supported for
! UNLOPS (ickkw=4).
! Rerun integration/grid setup after changing this setting.
#FKSExplicitSum
.false.
! Default :: .false.
!
! ==========================================================================
! FxFx analytic Sudakov finite terms (ickkw=3 only).
! .false.: the standard logarithmic NLL kernels.
! .true.: massless forward splitting kernels integrated with Pythia8's
! momentum tagging and global ISR z bound, identifying the upper FxFx
! scale with the dipole mass. Retains A1, B1, A2 and the existing massive
! terms. Includes the same finite terms in the NLO expansion subtraction.
! This universal prescription omits event-dependent PDFs, dipole recoil
! and matrix-element corrections; it is not a Pythia no-emission weight.
! Rerun integration/grid setup and event generation after changing it.
#FxFxPythia8FiniteTerms
.false.
! Default :: .false.
!
! ==========================================================================
! End of FKS_params.dat file
! ==========================================================================

NITERATIONS = 2
ACCURACY = 0.0001
ADAPT_GRID = 2
MULTICHANNEL = 1
SUM_HELICITY = 1
NCHANS = 4
CHANNEL = 1.1 1.2 2.1 2.2
SPLIT = 0
WGT_MULT= 1.0
RUN_MODE = all
RESTART = -1

! ==========================================================================
! This file sets the different technical parameters intrinsic to the
! FKS program and which controls the behaviour of the code at run
! time.  The common user should not edit this file and only experts
! should venture editing these parameters.
! ==========================================================================
!
! ==========================================================================
! Parameters controlling the tests based on the IR poles comparison
! ==========================================================================
!
! This threshold sets the limiting value for the comparison of the
! relative difference of the IR pole from the OLP and the one computed
! internaly by MadFKS.  The value below is used for the first PS
! points to assess the sanity of the computation. A value ten times
! smaller will be used for the systematic check of IR poles at
! runtime.
! Notice that the systematic comparison of IR poles at run time is
! only performed when the Monte-Carlo over helicity configurations
! method is not used.  Set this value to '-1.0d0' if you want the
! check to always pass.
#IRPoleCheckThreshold
1.0d-5
! Default :: 1.0d-5
!
! ==========================================================================
! OLP (virtuals) behavior at run time
! ==========================================================================
!
!
! Set the precision required from the OLP code. The IR poles check
! will be performed at run time with a threshold ten times loser than
! the value below. When equal to '-1d0' the default value of the OLP
! is used, and the poles check is disabled at run time
!
#PrecisionVirtualAtRunTime
1.0d-3
! Default :: 1.0d-3
!
! ==========================================================================
! Parameters controlling what coupling orders must be factorized by the
! contributions included by MadFKS in the context of mixed-order expansions
! ==========================================================================
!
! Set the QCD and QED squared order that must be factorized by the  
! contribution selected. This follows the same convention as the syntax 
! QCD^2== and QED^2== used at generation time. The default value of -1 
! instructs MadFKS to include all those available.
!
#QCD^2==
-1
! Default :: -1
!
#QED^2==
-1
! Default :: -1
!
! Alternatively the user can defined a list of squared orders to select
! The first entry is the number of specifed squared orders, and the ordering
! is indicated in orders.inc with typically QCD first, followed by QED
! This is just the generalization of the short-hand above.
!
! Example:
!
! #SelectedCouplingOrders
! 2
! 4 0
! 2 2
!
! Selects all contribution factorizing \alpha_s^2 and \alpha_s * \alpha.
!
#SelectedCouplingOrders
0
-1 -1
! Default ::
! 0
! -1 -1
!
! ==========================================================================
! This parameter allows to veto of select specific type of contributions.
!     type=1 : real-emission
!     type=2 : Born
!     type=3 : integrated counter terms
!     type=4 : soft counter-term
!     type=5 : collinear counter-term
!     type=6 : soft-collinear counter-term
!     type=7 : O(alphaS) expansion of Sudakov factor for NNLL+NLO
!     type=8 : soft counter-term (with n+1-body kin.)
!     type=9 : collinear counter-term (with n+1-body kin.)
!     type=10: soft-collinear counter-term (with n+1-body kin.)
!     type=11: real-emission (with n-body kin.)
!     type=12: MC subtraction with n-body kin.
!     type=13: MC subtraction with n+1-body kin.
!     type=14: virtual corrections
!     type=15: virt-trick: average born contribution
! ==========================================================================
! 
! The first entry specifies the length  of the list of vetoed or allowed types
!
! Example:
! #SelectedContributionTypes
! 3
! 2 14 15
!
! Would select only the finite part of the virtual and the Born contribution, and
!
! #VetoedContributionTypes
! 1
! 2
!
! Would remove the Born contribution, effectively computing only the NLO contribs.
!
! The default values disable completely these filters.
!
#VetoedContributionTypes
0
-1
! Default ::
! 0
! -1
!
#SelectedContributionTypes
0
-1
! Default :: .true.
! 0
! -1
!
! ==========================================================================
! Parameters defining the techniques used for the MC integration
! ==========================================================================
!
! This integer sets what is the minimum number of contributing
! helicities (in a given subrpocess) which is necessary for MadFKS to
! switch to the Monte-Carlo over helicity configurations method. Set
! this to '-1' if you want to forbid the use of this method
! altogether.
#NHelForMCoverHels
4
! Default :: 4
!
! This parameter sets for which fraction of the events the virtual
! matrix elements should be included. When using MINT, during the
! grid-setup phase, this number will be updated automatically after
! each iteration depending on the relative MC uncertainties.
#VirtualFraction
1.0d0
! Default :: 1.0d0
!
! This parameter sets the minimal fraction of the events for which the
! virtual matrix elements should be included.
#MinVirtualFraction
0.005d0
! Default :: 0.005d0
!
! Use a polynomial fit for the virtual corrections. Gets a better accuracy,
! but uses more memmory and disk space.
#UsePolyVirtual
.False.
! Default :: .True.
!
! ==========================================================================
! Combination of matrix elements
! ==========================================================================
!
! For fixed order calculations only (ignored for (N)LO+PS runs): This
! parameter determines if parton flavour configurations with idential
! matrix elements should be separated at the level of the analysis or
! not (these contributions are typically added together in
! parton_lum_?.f files and only the PDG info of the first contribution
! is passed to the analysis). This can be useful to tag e.g. b-jets in
! the case of a 5FS calculation. [Warning: in this case jets that
! contain both a b quark and a bbar quark should not be considered
! b-jet]. Setting this to .true. makes the code slower, in particular
! for complicated analyses as well as when doing reweighting for many
! scales and PDFs sets, since they have to be done for each flavour
! configuration separately.
#SeparateFlavourConfigurations
.false.
! Default :: .false.
!
! ==========================================================================
! Mapping for initial-state FKS emitters
! ==========================================================================
!
! 0: automatic (currently the asymmetric mapping in all run modes).
! 1: the original symmetric mapping, available without shower matching.
! 2: the asymmetric, Pythia-like mapping (only the emitting Bjorken x changes).
! A forced symmetric mapping with shower matching is rejected. The same
! choice is used for the real point, its counterevents, inverse projection,
! and the lepton recoil chart without event projection.
#FKSISRMapping
0
! Default :: 0
!
! ==========================================================================
! Recoil choice for final-state FKS emitters
! ==========================================================================
!
! 0: use the resonance's final-state decay system when available, or
!    the complete final-state recoil system otherwise (default).
! 1: use incoming particle 1 as the local recoiler.
! 2: use incoming particle 2 as the local recoiler.
! Initial-state recoil requires two incoming particles and a massless
! selected parton from a hadron beam (abs(lpp)=1 or 2). Its Bjorken x
! increases during radiation; the other final-state spectators keep
! their momenta. This option is supported for fixed-order calculations.
! Initial-state emitters keep their ordinary FKS map.
#FKSFinalRecoil
0
! Default :: 0
!
! ==========================================================================
! MC@NLO construction
! ==========================================================================
!
! Upper photon-conversion mass in PYTHIA8 QED MC subtraction (GeV).
! The shower launch script uses the same value for TimeShower:mMaxGamma.
! Rerun integration/grid setup after changing this setting.
#Pythia8MMaxGamma
10d0
! Default :: 10d0
!
! Use the refactored MC@NLO construction.  In this mode the complete
! explicit sum over native (kl) histories is formed before multiplying
! H-event subtraction terms by the outer S_ij function.
! Set .false. to use the standard native-sector MC@NLO matching.
#MCExplicitKLSum
.true.
! Default :: .true.
!
! Choose how Born colour flows enter the MC@NLO subtraction in both
! H and S events. With .true., evaluate at a sampled Born flow and apply
! its sampling weight (the current prescription). With .false., explicitly
! sum the MC counterterms over Born flows before combining event weights.
! The flow sum uses this branch's matching kernels and phase-space maps;
! it does not restore all matching choices of the 3.x series.
! Event colours and shower scales use this branch's sampled Born owner;
! the sum includes each flow's soft replacement and MC@NLO-Delta factor.
! Summed mode costs one native evaluation per leading Born flow.
! Independent of MCExplicitKLSum and FKSExplicitSum. Ignored at fixed order.
! Rerun integration/grid setup after changing this setting.
#MCSubtractionAtFixedFlow
.true.
! Default :: .true.
!
! Explicitly sum the outer FKS configurations at each integration point
! in NLO+PS runs, instead of sampling a group of configurations. The Born
! contribution is included once; S-event terms are combined before taking
! absolute values for unweighting. This can reduce negative weights at the
! cost of more matrix-element evaluations per point. Uses a common Born
! sampling chart so that the S events have identical underlying momenta.
! Any separate initial/final-state integration channels remain separate.
! Independent of MCExplicitKLSum (the inner matching-history sum).
! Requires event projection. Ignored at fixed order; not supported for
! UNLOPS (ickkw=4).
! Rerun integration/grid setup after changing this setting.
#FKSExplicitSum
.false.
! Default :: .false.
!
! ==========================================================================
! FxFx analytic Sudakov finite terms (ickkw=3 only).
! .false.: the standard logarithmic NLL kernels.
! .true.: massless forward splitting kernels integrated with Pythia8's
! momentum tagging and global ISR z bound, identifying the upper FxFx
! scale with the dipole mass. Retains A1, B1, A2 and the existing massive
! terms. Includes the same finite terms in the NLO expansion subtraction.
! This universal prescription omits event-dependent PDFs, dipole recoil
! and matrix-element corrections; it is not a Pythia no-emission weight.
! Rerun integration/grid setup and event generation after changing it.
#FxFxPythia8FiniteTerms
.false.
! Default :: .false.
!
! ==========================================================================
! End of FKS_params.dat file
! ==========================================================================

NPOINTS = 65536
NITERATIONS = 2
ACCURACY = 0.0001
ADAPT_GRID = 2
MULTICHANNEL = 1
SUM_HELICITY = 1
NCHANS = 4
CHANNEL = 1.1 1.2 2.1 2.2
SPLIT = 0
WGT_MULT= 1.0
RUN_MODE = all
RESTART = -1
